newsitem.title: PERU: Peru preparing "all-inclusive proposal" for rebels.
newsitem.headline: Peru preparing "all-inclusive proposal" for rebels.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori said on Tuesday the government was preparing an "all-inclusive proposal" to Marxist rebels who have rejected government moves to lure them into asylum to end a 77-day-old hostage siege.

Fujimori spoke in the southern city of Arequipa hours after guerrilla leader Nestor Cerpa dashed government hopes that he and his 20-odd comrades would accept one-way tickets to Cuba in return for dropping their main demands.

The president said the government was not giving up either the search for a bloodless end to the crisis or its stance against ceding to the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) demands for the release of 400 jailed comrades.

"His (Cerpa's) reactions are known publicly and we are not going to respond to his reactions," Fujimori said. "The government is preparing an all-inclusive proposal as a result of the talks that have been held in seven or eight meetings."

Cerpa said earlier on a walkie-talkie conversation monitored by Reuters that the eight rounds of talks between rebels and the government have so far led only to both sides stating their positions and that no progress had been made toward a deal.

He ruled out accepting a possible offer for asylum in the Dominican Republic but refused to comment on Monday's offer of sanctuary by Cuban leader Fidel Castro. He said the rebels were sticking to their demand for the release of prisoners.
"There has been no proposal for an amnesty (for rebels) presented to Congress and no proposal for an amnesty for the MRTA prisoners," he said.
A ninth round of talks is set for Wednesday.
The MRTA are holding 72 hostages -- including Fujimori's brother Pedro, two government ministers and the envoys of Japan and Bolivia -- in the Japanese ambassador's Lima residence.
